methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Endurance Energy is a SPAC-stage climate and energy company founded by Andrew Redd, having raised $5M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set presents material limitations for quantitative analysis.

The peer-median method is not applicable in this case. A review of same-stage and adjacent-stage peers within similar valuation tiers yielded fewer than three datapoints, the minimum threshold required for meaningful median-based valuation. While eight companies operate in the same sector, none meet the intersection of stage-specificity and tier-comparability needed to ground a reliable multiple. Applying an all-sector median would introduce excessive error given the heterogeneity of business models, capital requirements, and commercialization timelines across the broader Climate & Energy landscape.

Given these constraints, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range with confidence. The SPAC stage and limited peer density at comparable maturity levels create substantial uncertainty. A credible valuation would require either: (1) obtaining detailed financial and operational metrics from the identified private peers to enable multiples-based analysis; (2) gathering management guidance on near-term milestones and financing plans; or (3) awaiting disclosure of transaction terms if a SPAC merger is imminent. Until such data materializes, quantitative valuation anchors cannot be responsibly established.
